questions.question: Explain how HTML5 client-side form validation works in the browser and give at least four built-in validation attributes with a short example for each. Also explain why server-side validation is still necessary even when using HTML5 validation.
questions.expected_answer:
HTML5 form validation is performed by the browser before the form is submitted. The browser checks form controls against built-in constraints (attributes) and prevents submission if constraints fail, showing a default validation message. Developers can use attributes to declare requirements declaratively and can customize behavior using the Constraint Validation API (e.g., setCustomValidity) or disable built-in checks with the form's novalidate attribute.

Four built-in validation attributes with examples:
1) required — ensures a field is not empty. Example: <input name="email" type="email" required> (user must enter a value).
2) type — enforces a basic data type/format like email, number, url. Example: <input type="email" name="email"> (browser checks for an @ and valid email format).
3) pattern — enforces a regex pattern. Example: <input type="text" name="zip" pattern="\d{5}" title="Five-digit ZIP"> (must be exactly 5 digits).
4) minlength / maxlength — enforce character count limits. Example: <input type="password" name="pwd" minlength="8" maxlength="64">.
(Other useful ones: min/max/step for number/date inputs.)

Why server-side validation is still necessary:
- Client-side validation can be bypassed (disabled JavaScript, crafted HTTP requests, or modified HTML), so it cannot be trusted for security.
- Server-side validation ensures data integrity, enforces business rules, prevents injection attacks, and provides a reliable single source of truth for validation logic.
- Typically, use client-side validation for user experience (immediate feedback) and server-side validation for security and correctness.
questions.followup_question: Would you like a brief explanation now of how HTML5 form validation works, four example attributes with code snippets, and why server-side validation is still necessary?
questions.feedback: Candidate provided no substantive answer (only "i don't know" / "i do not know"). Missing explanation of how HTML5 validation works (browser constraint checking, Constraint Validation API, novalidate), no examples of built-in attributes (required, type, pattern, minlength/maxlength, min/max/step), and no reasons why server-side validation is necessary (bypassability, security, data integrity, business rules).

questions.question: The HTML form below should validate the email and submit the form, but clicking the 'Send' button neither triggers browser validation nor submits. Find the bug and provide the minimal fix so built-in HTML5 validation runs and the form can submit.
questions.expected_answer:
Bug: The button has type="button", which does not submit the form or trigger built-in HTML validation. Fix: change the button to type="submit" (or use <input type="submit">). Corrected code:

<form action="/subscribe" method="post">
  <label for="email">Email:</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required>
  <button id="send" type="submit">Send</button>
</form>

Explanation: Buttons with type="button" are inert and do not submit the form. Using type="submit" causes the browser to run HTML5 validation and submit the form if validation passes.
questions.feedback: Correct minimal fix — changing the button to type="submit" is exactly what’s needed so the browser runs HTML5 validation and submits the form. A brief explanatory note (that type="button" is inert and type="submit" triggers validation) would make the answer complete.
